contract.interface:
For finite H_S tensor H_B, d=dim(H_S), H=I_S tensor K+V with Hermitian K,V and ||V||op<=v, all subsystem-only terms and subsystem-bath coupling belong in V. At beta>0 let rho=exp(-beta H)/Z and X=x tensor I_B for any possibly non-Hermitian x. No bath dimension, bath energy scale, geometry, gap, commutation or mixing restriction is assumed. The claimed local KMS bound is K_rho(X)=Tr(sqrt(rho)X^dagger sqrt(rho)X)>=4 exp(-4 beta v)||x||op^2/(9d)>=4 exp(-4 beta v)Tr_S(x^dagger x)/(9d^2). This is a quadratic form, not ordinary uncentered variance or a transport coefficient. When v=0 it is exactly Tr_S(x^dagger x)/d.

More generally, lambda>sqrt(3) gives (1-3/lambda^2)^2 exp[-(lambda+1)beta v]||x||op^2/d. The singular-profile extension for lambda>0 replaces the numerator by sum_a(s_a(x)-3||x||op/lambda^2)_+^2. For Hermitian A,B with ||A-B||<=v, low/high spectral projections separated by g obey ||QP0||<=v/g, using a Sylvester integral. If X commutes with P0, compression error is <=3||QP0||^2||X||. Applied to I tensor K versus H, each low bath level supplies a copy of x; retained singular values after widening by lambda v are thermally integrated and divided by the scalar min-max bound Z<=d exp(beta v)Z_B. No false operator-order monotonicity of exp or efficient spectral-projector access is assumed.

The finite-band form K_{rho,Omega}(X)=sum_{|E_i-E_j|<=Omega}sqrt(p_i p_j)|X_ij|^2 obeys K_{rho,7v}(X)>=exp(-5 beta v)||x||op^2/(72d). Width-v bath windows enlarged by 3v on each side and a bounded overlap count supply this absolute floor. It is not a constant fraction of all KMS weight, excludes no zero-frequency contribution, and gives no nonzero-frequency absorption, conductivity, rapid mixing or finite-resolution measurement algorithm.

For Hermitian A centered at its thermal mean, BKM covariance dominates KMS. Static susceptibility is at least (4beta/(9d))exp(-4beta v) Var_tauS(A). For traceless local basis F_a with tauS(F_a F_b)=delta_ab, fixed bath K and fixed coupling V0, and ||V0+sum h_a F_a tensor I||<=v throughout a convex parameter region, Hessian(log Z)>=beta^2 kappa I, kappa=4exp(-4beta v)/(9d). Thus ||h-h'||_2<=(9d/(4beta))exp(4beta v)||m(h)-m(h')||_2. This is conditional local-field identifiability with fixed environment, not identification of an unknown bath/coupling. The explicit commuting h Z_S+b Z_B+J Z_S Z_B example gives indistinguishable local Gibbs states for different h when bath/coupling vary.

With q bounded observables ||F_a||<=L, supplied independent exact equilibrium copies, and a fit with stated residual, the note gives the sufficient count q+81q^2 L^2 d^2 exp(8beta v)log(2q/alpha)/(2beta^2 epsilon^2) for parameter error epsilon. It does not efficiently compute the expectation map, log Z or the fit. Copy preparation costs multiply this count by the actual T_eq; independence, preparation bias, measurement implementation and optimization remain charged. The theorem supplies no Gibbs sampler or equilibrium-time bound.

The low-temperature qubit H=hZ has susceptibility beta sech^2(beta h)~4beta exp(-2beta v), so universal polynomial-beta-v conditioning is impossible; exponent constants are not claimed optimal. For even d>=4, an explicit bath of dimension d-1, M=4log d, r=2/(sqrt(M^2+4)+M), local traceless Hermitian x=diag(1,-1,r^2,-r^2,...) and norm-one disjoint two-by-two perturbations gives beta=v=1, thermal mean zero, K<=3/d and tauS(x^2)>=1/[2(4log d+1)^4]. Their ratio tends to zero. This excludes a dimension-free KMS-to-tracial comparison in this general class, not a fixed-locality bounded-degree global covariance theorem or a dimension-free impossibility for BKM itself.

For k-qubit support with incident interaction norm sum <=gk, d=2^k,v<=gk yields ||X||tau <=(3/2)2^(k/2)exp(2beta gk)||X||rho,KMS. The source compares this linear-beta exponent with Chen--Anshu--Nguyen arXiv:2504.02706v1 Lemma III.6 and Bergamaschi arXiv:2610.01074v1 Lemma 3.6, which have beta log(beta) behavior in the specified inequalities. This is not exhaustive novelty clearance or a complete learning-algorithm speedup. The desired global BKM covariance bound Cov(sum u_a P_a,sum u_a P_a)>=c(beta,J,k,Delta)sum u_a^2 independent of size/term count remains open. Applying a local bound to the whole support makes d exponential and v extensive; positive termwise variances do not control off-diagonal cancellation. Learning-SYK arXiv:2610.02178v1 retains an explicit term-count denominator in the cited comparison.
